contract.words: Earn $1,500 a month in recurring revenue within 45 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: Recurring revenue of $1,500 a month in place within 45 days: recurring monthly agreements totalling at least $1,500/month, with a monthly payment settled inside the window

strategy.title: Bill the six agreed brewery TTB clients for month one and sell four vet reconciliation workbooks
strategy.why: Six written acceptances at $300/month for TTB excise report preparation give $1,800 settling day 16 (15 days to first cash); only month one settles inside the 30-day window, so month two is not counted. Four $450 vet controlled-substance workbooks ($1,800) to the 1,200 licensed clinics, at an evidenced 12% paid conversion and 4 days to first cash, bring the total to $3,600 gross, $3,530 after $70 direct costs. Brain produces every spreadsheet; payment is taken before delivery so no capital is exposed.

alternatives.title: Vet workbooks alone (7 deals, $3,150)
alternatives.why: Viable on the evidence but rests entirely on new sales; the brewery acceptances cut new sales needed to four.

alternatives.title: Brewery alone
alternatives.why: Rejected: six agreed clients x $300 = $1,800 in-window; the second monthly bill settles after day 30 and new brewery sales have no evidenced conversion.

Brain produces and delivers the four reconciliation workbooks

strategy.title: Start the six agreed brewery clients on $300/month TTB report preparation ($1,800/month recurring)
strategy.why: The goal now counts a monthly recurring run-rate of $1,500 within 45 days. Six written acceptances at $300 a month, billed monthly, give $1,800/month of recurring revenue (six clients; five would be exactly $1,500, the sixth is margin). The first monthly payment settles 15 days after invoicing (day 16), inside the 45-day window; Brain produces each monthly spreadsheet ($10 direct cost) after payment, so no capital is exposed. The one-off vet workbook does not move a monthly run-rate and is excluded.
